prior_findings.claim: A one-line custom rule can be mistaken for the legacy template: is_pure_omarchy_fontconfig deletes whole <string> lines during normalization, so the setter deletes fonts.conf and the migration deletes it when the drop-in already exists, losing the custom rule.
prior_findings.reason: Both reviewers independently reproduced the original loss at 69220f1 (setter and migration with drop-in present) and observed the one-line serif file preserved byte-identically at a1d2e51 by the setter and by the migration with the drop-in present or absent; a pure legacy file is still retired. The original claim was accurate. One understatement: with the drop-in absent at 69220f1 the copied rule was lost at the next omarchy-font-set run (both reviewers, Sol follow-up Q2).

Greedy s/<!--.*-->//g in both is_pure_omarchy_fontconfig copies erases a live custom rule placed between two comments on the same line, so a mixed file is classified pure: setter deletes fonts.conf, migration deletes it when the drop-in exists, and when absent the copied drop-in is overwritten at the next set. Present at both heads (not introduced by a1d2e51). Found independently by both reviewers. Opus tested s/<!--([^-]|-[^-])*-->//g across 22 variants: changes only this case and a pure template wrapped by two same-line comments.

When the setter keeps a mixed fonts.conf that still contains the legacy Omarchy monospace block, fontconfig 2.18.3's 50-user.conf includes conf.d before fonts.conf and both use prepend_first strong, so the old font resolves first for monospace; the setter reports nothing. Opus found it; Sol confirmed independently after a neutral follow-up question. Pre-existing for multi-line mixed files at 69220f1; a1d2e51 extends it to one-line mixed files that were previously deleted. Design limitation of the whole PR, not raised in the earlier review.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12935#issuecomment-5787369717) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12935#issuecomment-5788965606), checked at `a1d2e51fc544`.

**Verified: the earlier finding (one-line custom rule mistaken for the legacy template) is resolved.** Both `is_pure_omarchy_fontconfig` copies now strip only comments, the XML declaration, DOCTYPE, `<fontconfig>` tags and whitespace, then require the whole remainder to match the legacy block with only the font name free. With the one-line serif rule from the earlier review:

```text
                          69220f1d53d5           a1d2e51fc544
font set                  fonts.conf deleted     kept, byte-identical
migration, drop-in exists fonts.conf deleted     kept, byte-identical
migration, no drop-in     copied to drop-in,     kept, byte-identical
                          lost at next font set
pure legacy file          retired                retired
```

The earlier review understated the last case: without a drop-in, the copied rule was lost at the next `omarchy font set`, because the setter overwrites the drop-in. The new detector also keeps a custom rule that shares a line with `<fontconfig>` or `</fontconfig>`, or that carries a single leading or trailing comment; the previous detector dropped those too. The PR's test file passes 9/9, and its new setter and migration-with-drop-in cases fail against the previous scripts.

Two points remain. Neither was introduced by `a1d2e51`.

## Two comments on one line still hide a custom rule

The comment strip `s/<!--.*-->//g` ([setter](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/a1d2e51fc54400d3f955ac49b1f7f4a617522fca/bin/omarchy-font-set#L57-L64), [migration](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/a1d2e51fc54400d3f955ac49b1f7f4a617522fca/migrations/1790098827.sh#L11-L18)) is greedy. On one line it removes everything from the first `<!--` to the last `-->`, including any live rule in between. This synthetic line, added after the multiline legacy block, is therefore ignored during classification:

```xml
<!-- serif override --><match target="pattern"><test name="family" qual="any"><string>serif</string></test><edit name="family" mode="prepend_first" binding="strong"><string>Alternate Serif</string></edit></match><!-- end -->
```

The file is then treated as pure: the setter deletes `fonts.conf`, the migration deletes it when the drop-in exists, and without a drop-in the copied rule is lost at the next `omarchy font set`. The same behavior exists at `69220f1d53d5`. It is a narrow exception to the reply's "regardless of line breaks or formatting".

**Impact:** silent loss of a custom rule, limited to a whole rule on one line with comments on both sides.

**Suggested change:** use a non-greedy comment pattern in both copies, for example `s/<!--([^-]|-[^-])*-->//g` (XML comments cannot contain `--`). Across 22 synthetic `fonts.conf` variants this changed only the case above (now kept) and a pure template wrapped by two comments on one line (now retired). Adding the two-comment case to the preservation tests would cover it.

## A kept `fonts.conf` with the old Omarchy block still overrides the new font

When `fonts.conf` is kept because it contains extra rules, its legacy monospace block stays active. fontconfig's `50-user.conf` includes `~/.config/fontconfig/conf.d` before `fonts.conf`, and both rules use `prepend_first`, so the later (old) font lands first:

```text
fontconfig 2.18.3 default chain + 50-omarchy.conf, after `omarchy font set` to a new font

drop-in only (or pure legacy file retired)  ->  monospace: New Font, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font, ...
drop-in + kept mixed fonts.conf             ->  monospace: Old Legacy Font, New Font, ...
```

The setter exits 0 and prints nothing about it. This already applied at `69220f1d53d5` to mixed files written across several lines; `a1d2e51` extends it to one-line mixed files, which were previously deleted.

**Impact:** for users whose `fonts.conf` holds the old Omarchy block plus their own rules, `omarchy font set` updates terminal configs and the drop-in, but fontconfig `monospace` (including the shell's `fc-match` lookup) keeps preferring the old font, with no indication why. Keeping the file is the safer choice; the gap is the silent result.

**Suggested change:** when a kept `fonts.conf` still contains a `monospace` family edit, print or send a short notice naming the block to remove, or document the step.

---

**Test scope:** real setter and migration scripts at both heads in isolated synthetic homes, with unrelated setter effects stubbed; the PR's own test file; fontconfig 2.18.3 `fc-pattern` preference order under a synthetic copy of its default configuration chain plus Omarchy's `50-omarchy.conf`, never the host configuration. The override result depends on the linked default rules and was not checked on other fontconfig versions. No desktop, QML or native font rendering validation; the author's VM result was not reproduced.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, with independent technical assessments by Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh.
